paragraphs.title: The Construction and Structure of Solomon’s Palace

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says Solomon was building his own house thirteen years.
easy.q: How many years did Solomon build his own house?

easy.explanation: It was built upon four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams.
easy.q: What was the House of the Forest of Lebanon built largely with?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says it stood upon four rows of cedar pillars.
easy.q: How many rows of cedar pillars supported the House of the Forest of Lebanon?

medium.q: How high was the House of the Forest of Lebanon?

answers: Large hewed stones used in construction
medium.explanation: The costly stones were great hewed and sawed stones used from the foundation upward.
medium.q: What does “costly stones” describe in these verses?

answers: It included open spaces and courts
medium.explanation: The passage mentions a great court and other courts around the buildings.
medium.q: What does the description of the great court show about the palace design?

answers: It had a carefully planned, multi-level structure
challenge.explanation: The three rows of windows point to a large and carefully arranged building.
challenge.q: What does the mention of windows in three rows suggest about the House of the Forest of Lebanon?

answers: To show it was made of brass
To show similarity in design and workmanship
To show that it was smaller
challenge.explanation: The verse compares its construction with the porch previously described.
challenge.q: Why is Pharaoh’s daughter’s house said to be “like unto this porch”?

answers: The construction used several building materials
The cedar replaced all the stones
The stones were used only to make tools
challenge.explanation: The passage describes both cedar and hewed stones as parts of the buildings.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from cedar beams to hewed stones?

easy.explanation: Solomon sent and fetched Hiram out of Tyre.
easy.q: Whom did Solomon send for from Tyre?

easy.explanation: Hiram cast two pillars of brass.
easy.q: What material did Hiram use to make the two pillars?

easy.explanation: The right pillar was called Jachin and the left pillar Boaz.
easy.q: What were the names of the two pillars?

answers: Wisdom, understanding, and skill in working brass
The ability to build ships only
The ability to write only on golden tablets
medium.explanation: He was filled with wisdom, understanding, and skill to work all works in brass.

answers: Parts placed on top of the pillars
Stones at the base of the court
Tools used to measure the Temple
medium.explanation: The chapiters were made to be set upon the tops of the pillars.
The networks covered the chapiters, and the pomegranates formed part of their ornament.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the nets and pomegranates on the chapiters?

challenge.explanation: The passage mentions two rows of pomegranates around each network.
challenge.q: Which detail especially emphasizes the repeated decoration of the chapiters?

answers: They were prominent parts of the entrance
They were placed inside the basins
challenge.explanation: Their placement in the porch made them notable features of the Temple entrance.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the pillars being set up in the porch of the Temple?

answers: Each name belonged to a particular pillar
Both names belonged to the same pillar
The names belonged to the chapiters, not the pillars
challenge.explanation: The right pillar was called Jachin, and the left pillar was called Boaz.
challenge.q: What relationship did Jachin and Boaz have to the pillars?

paragraphs.title: The Sea, the Stands, and the Basins

easy.explanation: The passage describes the great vessel as a molten sea of brass.
easy.q: Of what was the molten sea made?
How many oxen supported the sea?

easy.explanation: Verse 27 says he made ten bases of brass.
easy.q: How many bases or stands were made?

answers: There was one laver on each base
All the lavers were inside the sea
The bases were used only as decoration
medium.explanation: Ten lavers were made, one upon each of the ten bases.
medium.q: What was the relationship between the bases and the lavers?

medium.explanation: The bases were wheeled bronze stands that supported the lavers.
medium.q: What were the bases in this passage?

answers: To show that the bases could be moved
To describe the decoration of the sea
To show that the bases were made of cedar
medium.explanation: The wheels and axletrees were structural features of the movable bases.
medium.q: Why are the wheels and axletrees described?

answers: Three toward each of the four directions
challenge.explanation: Three looked north, three west, three south, and three east.
challenge.q: How were the faces of the oxen arranged beneath the sea?

answers: They were made according to a uniform design
They were made from completely different materials
challenge.explanation: The repeated measure and size show standardized construction.
challenge.q: What does the fact that all ten bases had one casting, measure, and size suggest?

answers: Lions, oxen, cherubims, and palm trees
challenge.explanation: The borders and plates included lions, oxen, cherubims, and palm trees.
challenge.q: Which combination of decorations appears on the bases?

easy.explanation: Hiram made the lavers, the shovels, and the basons.
easy.q: Which vessels did Hiram make for Solomon?

easy.explanation: The summary says there were ten lavers on the bases.
easy.q: How many lavers were placed on the bases?

answers: In the House of the Forest of Lebanon
easy.explanation: They were cast in the plain of Jordan, between Succoth and Zarthan.
easy.q: Where were the bronze vessels cast?

answers: There were so many that their weight was not measured
medium.explanation: The vessels were exceeding many, so the weight of the brass was not found out.
medium.q: What does “Solomon left all the vessels unweighed” mean?

answers: The passage says Hiram made all the work for the house of the Lord
The passage says Hiram built the palace
The passage assigns the golden vessels to Hiram
medium.explanation: The verses summarize the vessels Hiram made for King Solomon.
medium.q: What connects the list of vessels with Hiram’s work?

answers: To specify part of the decoration of the pillars
To give the number of lavers
To measure the depth of the sea
medium.explanation: The pomegranates covered the two networks on the chapiters.
medium.q: Why are the four hundred pomegranates mentioned in the summary?

answers: They were cast at a special site in the Jordan plain
They were made inside the most holy place
challenge.explanation: The passage identifies the clay ground in the Jordan plain as the casting site.
challenge.q: What does the casting location reveal about the preparation of the vessels?

answers: By the many vessels and the brass that was not weighed
By the making of only one vessel
By the fact that everything was made of cedar
challenge.explanation: The numerous objects and immense amount of brass show the scale of the project.
challenge.q: How is the scale of the work shown in these verses?

answers: The summary gathers together items described earlier
The summary cancels the description of the pillars
The summary changes to the construction of the palace
challenge.explanation: The summary repeats the pillars, pomegranates, bases, lavers, sea, and oxen.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the detailed description and the summary verses?

paragraphs.title: The Golden Furnishings and Completion of the Temple Work

easy.explanation: The golden table was the table whereupon the shewbread was placed.
easy.q: Which golden item held the shewbread?

easy.explanation: There were five on the right side and five on the left.
easy.q: How many candlesticks were on the right and left sides?

answers: The things David his father had dedicated
easy.explanation: Solomon brought in the silver, gold, and vessels David had dedicated.
easy.q: What did Solomon bring into the treasuries of the house of the Lord?

answers: The altar, table, candlesticks, and service vessels
medium.explanation: The passage lists the golden altar, table, candlesticks, bowls, snuffers, basons, spoons, censers, and hinges.
medium.q: Which items are included among the golden furnishings?

answers: They were made of refined, valuable gold
The gold was locked in the treasury
The gold was placed inside brass
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the quality and preciousness of the material.
medium.q: What does “pure gold” indicate about the candlesticks and vessels?

answers: After the work was finished, the dedicated treasures were brought in
The treasures were brought in before construction began
The treasures were used to build Pharaoh’s daughter’s house
medium.explanation: After the work was ended, Solomon brought in David’s dedicated things.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between finishing the work and David’s treasures?

answers: The Temple equipment included different materials and functions
Every vessel was made of the same material
The golden vessels were used only to build the palace
challenge.explanation: The chapter first describes many brass furnishings and then lists the golden furnishings.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the distinction between the golden and brass vessels?

answers: To identify parts of the candlesticks and their service equipment
To give the number of pillars
challenge.explanation: They are listed among the golden items associated with the candlesticks.
challenge.q: Why are the flowers, lamps, and tongs mentioned?

answers: Making the furnishings, completing the work, and storing the dedicated treasures
Building the palace, casting brass, and dedicating the court
Choosing Hiram, building the Forest of Lebanon, and preparing stones
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the Temple furnishings to the completion of the work and the placement of David’s treasures.
challenge.q: What sequence brings the passage to its conclusion?
